newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. mulls trade case against Canada copyright law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mulls trade case against Canada copyright law.

text.p: The United States is considering taking trade action against Canada for its new copyright law, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Friday.

"We're very, very concerned about the unequal distribution of blank tape levies," she told reporters after a morning meeting with Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton. "This is a violation of national treatment, among other violations, and we are looking at the possibility of bringing a case on that matter."
She would not say which international trade forum the U.S. would consider for taking action against Canada.
Barshefsky, Eggleton and trade chiefs from the European Union and Japan are in Toronto for a two-day Quadrilateral group meeting to promote global trade liberalization.
But Eggleton insisted Canada's copyright law does not breach any international conventions.

The legislation imposes a tax on blank audio cassettes, with the revenue to be distributed to performers. But the royalties are not passed on to U.S. performers since the United States has not signed an international treaty on copyright.

"We've examined it very carefully to make sure it meets our obligations, and we're sure it does," Eggleton told reporters. "If they don't feel we are (meeting our obligations), they have the possibility to take it to a dispute panel."
Canada and the U.S. also thrashed through a discussion on Canada's wheat exports to the United States, Barshefsky said.
But Barshefsky stopped short of making a call for a cap on Canadian wheat, opting instead to request better market access for U.S. agricultural products.
"We discussed our concerns about Canadian grains which are entering the U.S. at very, very high levels, both for durum wheat and spring wheat," she told reporters.

She said U.S. and Canadian officials met a week ago to discuss how U.S. agricultural products could get better access to Canada. Another officials' meeting is planned for the end of May or early June, she said.
Eggleton reiterated that Canada was within its rights to export as much wheat as it wants to the United States.
"We don't see a problem or any need to talk about any limitations (on grain exports)," he said.
